skills.author: navapbc
skills.content:
# Parity Scan

A parity analysis tool that helps analysts identify and categorize differences between two system outputs to track parity during a migration.

## Commands

- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list` — List all tickets as JSON (`dso` is not a global CLI; always invoke via `.claude/scripts/dso`)
- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket show <id>` — Show full ticket details
- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket transition <id> <status>` — Update ticket status
- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket comment <id> <body>` — Add a comment to a ticket
- `make dev` — Start local dev environment (Next.js + Postgres via Docker Compose)
- `make stop` — Stop local dev environment
- `npm test` — Run Jest unit tests with coverage (80% lines, 60% branches enforced) — includes `unit` and `middleware` projects
- `npm run test:integration` — Run integration tests against Postgres (requires `POSTGRES_URL`)
- `npm run test:integration:auth` — Run auth integration tests against Postgres + Keycloak (requires `POSTGRES_URL`, `KEYCLOAK_URL`, `KEYCLOAK_REALM`, `APP_URL`)
- `npm run lint` — Run ESLint
- `npm run format` — Run Prettier
- `npm run format-check` — Check formatting without fixing
- `npm run ts:check` — TypeScript type check
- `npm run migrate` — Run database migrations
- `bash scripts/audit-env-drift.sh` — Diff env-var keys referenced in app code against Terraform task definition; exits 0 if no undocumented drift
- `gh workflow run deploy-staging.yml` — Trigger a manual staging deploy via GitHub Actions (requires `gh` CLI authenticated to the repo)
- `TF_VAR_db_password=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id /parity-scan/staging/db_password --region us-east-2 --query SecretString --output text) terraform -chdir=infra/terraform apply` — Apply Terraform infrastructure changes to staging (requires AWS credentials)

> **Important:** `gh workflow run deploy-staging.yml` only deploys the Docker image — it does NOT run `terraform apply`. Infrastructure changes (ECS task definition env vars, Cognito client settings, ALB listeners, RDS, IAM, etc.) require a separate `terraform apply` run. Always apply Terraform first when `infra/terraform/` files change, then trigger the deploy workflow to pick up the new task definition.

> **Staging operations:** See `docs/staging-operations.md` for the full runbook — architecture, user provisioning (Cognito), diagnostic commands, and the documented list of critical non-obvious configuration (AUTH_URL requirement, CloudFront origin timeout, the reason `i18nMiddleware` is not invoked, Dockerfile USWDS asset copy, etc.).

## Architectural Invariants

These rules protect core structural boundaries. Violating them causes subtle bugs that are hard to trace.

1. **SQL Query Isolation** — All SQL queries (`sql` template literals from the postgres library) must live in `src/app/lib/data.ts` or `src/app/lib/migrate.ts`. No other file may contain SQL. See ADR-001.

2. **API Input Validation** — All API endpoints in `src/app/api/` that accept POST requests must validate the request body and return HTTP 400 with a descriptive error for invalid input. See ADR-003.

3. **Import Format Contract** — Import format handlers must implement a common processing pipeline: parse → map fields (optional, per-source schema mapping) → hash PII → store via data layer → trigger diff creation. New formats must not skip any step. See ADR-002.

4. **Layer Boundaries** — UI components in `src/components/` must not import directly from `src/app/lib/data.ts`. Components receive data through page/view server components or API routes, not by calling the data layer directly.

5. **Pattern Category Validation** — Pattern categories must be validated against `VALID_CATEGORIES` in `src/app/lib/constants.ts` before any database write. The allowed set is `under_investigation`, `known_bug`, `legacy_wrong`, `uncategorized`. Category values must not be accepted from user input without this server-side check. See ADR-004.

6. **Middleware Auth Boundary** — `src/middleware.ts` must not import `src/app/lib/bearerAuth.ts`. Bearer token resolution requires Postgres access and runs only in the Node.js runtime; middleware runs in the Edge runtime. API routes may call `bearerAuth` directly. See ADR-005.

7. **Role Validation** — User roles must be validated against `VALID_ROLES` in `src/app/lib/constants.ts` before any RBAC decision or database write. The allowed set is `viewer`, `analyst`, `admin`. Role values must not be accepted from user input without this server-side check.

8. **Pull Adapter Bundling** — `ibm_db` and `@aws-sdk/client-s3` must be listed in `serverExternalPackages` in `next.config.js`. Both are native or large SDK packages that must load from `node_modules` at runtime; webpack/Turbopack bundling will cause them to fail. See ADR-006.

9. **Project Context Isolation** — `src/app/lib/projectContext.ts` must not be imported by `src/middleware.ts`. It calls `isMember()` from the data layer, which requires Postgres access and runs only in the Node.js runtime. API route handlers call `resolveProjectFromHeader` directly after auth succeeds. See ADR-007.

10. **Raw Payload Storage Enforcement** — `shouldStorePayload()` in `src/app/lib/data.ts` guards all three raw storage functions (`storeRequest`, `storeResponse`, `storeAdditionalContext`). Suppression uses a conjunction: storage is suppressed only when `raw_storage_enabled = false` AND the project has at least one PII field configured. When `raw_storage_enabled` is `null` (legacy projects), `true`, or `false` with no PII fields configured, storage proceeds. New storage functions must call `shouldStorePayload()` before writing.

11. **Bottleneck Rate Limiting Configuration** — `BOTTLENECK_MAX_QUEUE` must be set as an environment variable and is validated at startup in `src/instrumentation.ts` (must be a positive integer; missing or invalid values cause a fast-fail error). Pull adapters (`src/app/lib/db2Import.ts`, `src/app/lib/s3Import.ts`) read `BOTTLENECK_MAX_QUEUE_VALUE` from instrumentation for their queue high-water mark. Per-adapter `Bottleneck` instances are lazily instantiated — created only when a source's `rate_limit_rps` field is set.

12. **Security Header Injection Strategy** — `X-Frame-Options` and `X-Content-Type-Options` are set unconditionally via `next.config.js` `headers()` (applied to all routes by Next.js before middleware runs). HSTS is set conditionally in `src/middleware.ts` `applyHSTS()` (production + HTTPS only, applied after `i18nMiddleware`). CSP nonce is set via `src/middleware.ts` `withNonce()` on every return path in the middleware handler (applied after `i18nMiddleware` to prevent next-intl from stripping the header). See ADR-009.

13. **CSP Nonce Per-Request Uniqueness and PPR Prohibition** — A fresh nonce is generated per request using `crypto.randomUUID()` in `src/middleware.ts`. `withNonce()` must wrap every return path in the middleware handler. PPR (Partial Pre-Rendering) must remain disabled in `next.config.js`; enabling PPR allows middleware output to be cached and reused across requests, which would cause nonce reuse and invalidate the CSP security property. This constraint is enforced by `tests/architecture/security-config.test.ts`. See ADR-010.

14. **Translation Layer Server-Side Boundary** — `src/app/lib/queryBuilderTranslation.ts` must not be imported by any file in `src/components/`.

15. **Auth Provider Fail-Fast Validation** — `AUTH_PROVIDER` must be set to `keycloak` or `cognito` (exact string, no whitespace, case-sensitive). `src/instrumentation.ts` validates this at startup and fails fast with a descriptive error for unset, unrecognized, or malformed values. When `AUTH_PROVIDER=cognito`, `COGNITO_CLIENT_ID`, `COGNITO_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `COGNITO_ISSUER` must also be set; `COGNITO_ISSUER` must be a well-formed HTTPS URL. See ADR-011.

16. **Migration Serialization via Advisory Lock** — `runMigrations()` in `src/app/lib/migrate.ts` acquires `pg_advisory_xact_lock(MIGRATION_LOCK_ID)` at the start of each migration transaction. This prevents two ECS tasks from concurrently applying the same migration during a blue-green deploy window (`deployment_minimum_healthy_percent = 100`). The lock is transaction-scoped and released automatically on commit or rollback. See ADR-012.

17. **RDS Safe-Default Snapshot Policy** — The staging RDS instance in `infra/terraform/` must be configured with `skip_final_snapshot = false` and `deletion_protection = true`. These are safe defaults: a final snapshot is created on destroy (preventing accidental data loss), and deletion protection requires an explicit manual override before `terraform destroy` can remove the instance. Do not change either setting without a deliberate, documented reason.

18. **`AUTH_URL` Required in ECS Task Definition** — `infra/terraform/ecs.tf` must set the `AUTH_URL` env var to `local.oauth_base_url` (the HTTPS CloudFront URL). Auth.js v5's `trustHost: true` alone is insufficient in containerized deployments — Auth.js falls back to the TCP bind address (`0.0.0.0:3000`) when `AUTH_URL` is unset because Next.js builds `req.url` from the socket, not from `X-Forwarded-Host`. Without `AUTH_URL`, Cognito receives `redirect_uri=http://0.0.0.0:3000/...` and rejects the flow with `error=Configuration`. Enforced by `tests/architecture/auth-url-ecs.test.ts`.

19. **`createIntlMiddleware` Must Not Be Invoked in `src/middleware.ts`** — With `AUTH_URL` set, Auth.js's `auth(handler)` wrapper makes `req.url` absolute with the `AUTH_URL` host. `createIntlMiddleware` then emits absolute `x-middleware-rewrite` headers, which Next.js treats as external proxies and fetches over HTTP — creating a CloudFront → ALB → CloudFront network-level request loop. Locale routing is handled instead by explicit redirects in `handler()` (for `/` and `/login`), and `setRequestLocale()` in `src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx` provides the locale to `getRequestConfig` directly from the route param. Re-introducing `i18nMiddleware` will re-introduce the loop.

20. **CloudFront HTTPS Fronts the HTTP-Only ALB** — The ALB has no ACM certificate (staging uses an auto-generated DNS name, not a custom domain). Public HTTPS is provided by a CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB (`infra/terraform/cloudfront.tf`). Cognito callback URLs (`local.oauth_base_url`) and `AUTH_URL` both derive from `aws_cloudfront_distribution.main.domain_name`. CloudFront `origin_read_timeout` is set to 180s (not the 30s default) so large synchronous server actions like CSV imports complete before the edge times out. Changing the origin to HTTPS requires adding an ACM cert to the ALB.

21. **No Shadow Routes Under `[locale]/`** — `src/app/[locale]/` may only contain an allowlisted set of immediate children (`[projectSlug]`, `__tests__`, `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx`, `login`, `no-membership`, `no-projects`, `projects`). Project-scoped features (`manage`, `patterns`, `edit`, `details`, `differences`, etc.) must live under `src/app/[locale]/[projectSlug]/` only. A feature directory at `src/app/[locale]/<feature>/page.tsx` creates a "shadow route": a slug-less URL like `/<slug>/<feature>` silently matches `[locale]=<slug>` and renders a broken page with project context lost (`useParams().locale === <slug>` poisons locale context across the page). Enforced by `tests/architecture/no-shadow-locale-routes.test.ts`. Adding a new immediate child requires updating both the test allowlist and this invariant with a written justification. See tickets `1182-dc56` (differences) and `21b0-b76b` (manage/patterns/edit/details).

22. **`"use server"` Module Purity** — Files whose first statement is `"use server"` are Next.js Server Action modules (currently `src/app/lib/data.ts`, `src/app/lib/savePattern.ts`, `src/app/lib/importActions.ts`, `src/app/lib/savePiiFields.ts`). Every value export from these files must be an `async function`. Non-async value exports — constants, arrays, objects, RegExp literals, classes, sync functions, and re-exports of any of these — are prohibited. At Server Action invocation time Next.js 15 throws `A "use server" file can only export async functions, found <type>` which surfaces to the client as a generic HTTP 500 "Server Components render error" with only a digest hash; the real cause is nearly invisible without server-side logs. TypeScript `export type { ... }` is permitted because type exports are erased at compile time. Pure utility helpers (validators, constants, sync pure functions) must live in sibling non-`"use server"` modules (e.g. `src/app/lib/sqlSchema.ts`, `src/app/lib/constants.ts`) and be imported into server-action files for internal use only — never re-exported from them. When adding a new server-action module, inspect every `export` statement before committing: the only permitted shapes are `export async function X(...)` and `export type { ... }`. See bug 9b73-f4ff (regression surfaced when adding a validator import chain).

23. **Email Lowercase Storage Contract** — All email values stored in the `project_members` table must be lowercased before insert or update. `addMember()` in `src/app/lib/data.ts` calls `email.trim().toLowerCase()` before the SQL INSERT. Read-path functions (`isMember()`, `listProjectsForUser()`, `listUserMemberships()`) use `lower(pm.email) = lower(${subject})` for case-insensitive lookup. This prevents silent membership mismatches when Auth.js (Keycloak/Cognito) returns lowercased session emails for addresses entered with mixed case by admins. Migration 015 normalizes existing rows via `applyEmailDeduplication()` in `migrate.ts`.

## Architecture

- **Monolith**: Single Next.js app with PostgreSQL database; schema-per-project isolation (`public` schema for cross-project tables; `[projectSlug]` schema for project-scoped tables). Deployed to AWS staging (ECS Fargate + RDS PostgreSQL) via Terraform; see `infra/terraform/README.md`
- **Data Layer**: `src/app/lib/data.ts` — all database access; project-scoped functions accept a `projectSchema` parameter
- **Auth**: `src/auth.ts` — Auth.js v5 config; provider-aware JWT strategy; provider selected at runtime by `AUTH_PROVIDER` env var (`keycloak` = local dev default, `cognito` = staging/production). Keycloak and Cognito providers both resolve to identical session shape via `normalizeClaimsToRole()`
- **Middleware**: `src/middleware.ts` — auth composition + RBAC `ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` matrix + project slug validation
- **Auth Utilities**: `src/app/lib/claimNormalizer.ts` (`AuthIdentity` includes optional `projectId`/`projectSlug` for API key auth), `src/app/lib/bearerAuth.ts`, `src/app/lib/auth/staleRole.ts`
- **Project Utilities**: `src/app/lib/projectContext.ts` — `resolveProjectFromHeader`; `src/app/lib/postLoginRouting.ts` — `resolvePostLoginRoute` (7-step priority chain)
- **Business Logic**: `src/app/lib/` — import, diff creation, pattern matching, schema field mapping (`schemaMapping.ts`); push import handlers: `CsvImportHandler` and `X12FlatImportHandler` in `src/app/lib/x12Import.ts` (parses X12 EDI flat files — 837I institutional claims and 837P professional claims — validated against `VALID_X12_TRANSACTION_TYPES` in `constants.ts`; supports both element-delimited and fixed-width formats; fixed-width path uses `PZMAP_837I` from `src/app/lib/pzmaps/837I.ts`, a position-map config defining byte offsets and field lengths for parsing fixed-width X12 flat file fields); pull adapters (`db2Import.ts`, `s3Import.ts`); FP-Growth frequent itemset mining (`fpgrowth.ts`) — pure TypeScript, zero external dependencies
- **API**: `src/app/api/` — endpoints for third-party client access, `/api/keys` for API key management, `/api/import-sources` for pull-adapter CRUD, `/api/import/db2` and `/api/import/s3` for pull triggers, `POST /api/suggestions` for pattern suggestions (analyst+ role, accepts `minSupport` and `maxLen` params), `PATCH /api/projects/[id]/members/[email]` for updating a member's role (admin only; validates against `VALID_ROLES`; prevents self-demotion with 403)
- **UI**: `src/app/[locale]/[projectSlug]/` project-scoped pages + `src/app/[locale]/projects` project management (admin) + `src/components/` — USWDS React components including `SuggestionCard` (accept/edit/dismiss suggestion actions), `JsonCriteriaBuilder` (graphical query builder using `react-querybuilder` with USWDS `controlElements`), and `ProjectManagement` (members table with inline USWDS Select for role editing; receives `currentUserEmail` prop threaded from `session.user.email.toLowerCase()` via `page.tsx` → `view.tsx` to disable self-role-change and exclude `@placeholder.local` placeholder members)
- **Graphical Query Builder**: `react-querybuilder` powers `src/components/JsonCriteriaBuilder.tsx`; added to `transpilePackages` in `next.config.js` (client component library — not `serverExternalPackages`). USWDS custom `controlElements` wrap builder controls with `@trussworks/react-uswds` components.
- **i18n**: English and Spanish via next-intl

## Testing

- Jest 30 with Testing Library and jest-axe for accessibility
- Jest projects array: `unit` (jsdom) and `integration` (node) — run independently via `--selectProjects`
- Architecture fitness tests in `tests/architecture/` enforce structural invariants
- Integration tests in `tests/integration/` — run against a live Postgres instance
- Coverage thresholds: 80% lines, 60% branches (enforced as CI gate on unit tests)
- Coverage scoped to `src/app/api/`, `src/app/lib/`, `src/components/`
- Test index at `.test-index` maps source files to their tests

## Design

- U.S. Web Design System (USWDS) via @trussworks/react-uswds
- WCAG AA accessibility target
- Visual language: Clean, Functional, Data-focused

skills.name: nj-ui-claude-starter
skills.description: Read and follow the personality instructions at `claude-personality.md` at the start of every session.
skills.author: navapbc
skills.content:
# Personality

Read and follow the personality instructions at `claude-personality.md` at the start of every session.

# Never share claimant PII with Claude

**Stop and think before pasting anything claimant-related into a Claude prompt, attached file, terminal output, or any other surface Claude can read.** A Claude conversation is a third-party data flow — anything that lands in a prompt has left the secure perimeter and cannot be recalled.

PII includes (non-exhaustive): SSNs, dates of birth, full names tied to a case, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, claim contents, employment history with employer names, monetary determinations tied to an individual, and case IDs that resolve to a real person via the database.

Do this instead:

- Use synthetic or scrubbed fixtures when debugging. Never paste a real claim, decision row, or audit log entry.
- When reproducing a production issue, scrub PII first: replace SSN with `XXX-XX-1234`, swap names, randomize DOBs, etc.
- If a stack trace or log line includes PII, redact before sharing it with Claude.
- If you can't share something safely, describe it in the abstract and attach a synthetic reproduction.

This rule has no exceptions. "Just this once" is how compliance violations happen. If you are unsure whether a piece of data counts, treat it as PII and redact.

# Stack defaults

NJ DOL ecosystem standards. Prefer the in-stack option unless there is a concrete reason not to — and name the trade-off when you go off-stack.

- **Frontend:** Next.js + React-USWDS, react-hook-form + Zod, Sass
- **Backend:** Python 3.11, AWS Lambda (monolambda pattern), SQLAlchemy + Alembic
- **Auth:** Cognito + OIDC (Azure AD federation)
- **LLM:** Claude via AWS Bedrock with chain-of-thought + RAG
- **IaC:** Terraform; **CI:** GitHub Actions; **Local dev:** docker-compose + LocalStack

# Accessibility

WCAG 2.1 AA and Section 508c are non-negotiable for any claimant-facing surface. Reach for USWDS components first; only build custom when USWDS genuinely doesn't cover it, and when you do, match USWDS color tokens, focus rings, and keyboard behavior.

# Plain language for claimant copy

Target 8th-grade reading level. Hints are *instructions* ("Enter your last day of work"), not *diagnoses* ("Invalid input"). Required-field markers must include text, not just asterisks. No government jargon — say "your last day of work," not "separation date."

# Spanish at parity, not as a follow-up

All user-facing strings live in i18n-keyed files. No hardcoded English in JSX or templates. Spanish copy preserves plain-language standards — if a phrase does not translate cleanly, work with reviewers, do not force a literal translation. NJ ships Spanish natively in production; new surfaces should not regress that.

# Audit-trail discipline

Decisions about claimant eligibility, payments, identity, or status are **append-only**. Never mutate or delete a Determination/decision row — write a corrective record instead. Each decision carries: facts at decision time, the rule version that produced it, the method (`automated | staff_review | attestation | override`), and a reasons tree. Flag any code that mutates decisions in place.

# Operational PII handling

Beyond the "never share with Claude" rule above: do not log raw claimant data to stdout, CloudWatch, or test fixtures. Use structured audit logs keyed by user/case IDs, never raw payloads. Tests use generated fake PII — never copy from production exports.

# AI attribution on commits

Use a `Co-Authored-By` trailer to note which AI tool was used on AI-assisted commits (per the NJ UI AI policy). You're still the author and you're still responsible for what ships; the trailer just records the tool involved.

skills.author: navapbc
skills.content:
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What This Repo Does

Automated project management hygiene checks and field updates for the **Strata** GitHub Project (navapbc org, project #4). Five workflows:

1. **Epic Hygiene Check** (`scripts/epic_hygiene_check.py`) — Daily cron that finds active epics (issueType=Epic, Roadmap Status=Now) missing owners or target dates, posts violations to Slack grouped by rule.
2. **Auto-fill Dates** (`.github/workflows/update-project-issue-dates.yml`) — Event-driven workflow that sets "Started on" when an issue moves to "In progress" and "Closed on" when moved to "Done".
3. **Draft Epic Status Updates** (`scripts/draft_epic_status_updates.py`) — Weekly cron (Mondays) that upserts a draft status-update row per active epic into the `Status updates` tab of the TSS weekly updates spreadsheet and notifies the epic owner via Slack.
4. **Publish Epic Status Summary** (`scripts/publish_epic_status_summary.py`) — Weekly cron (Thursdays) that reads the human-edited rows for the current week and posts a single grouped TSS-wide summary message to Slack.
5. **Publish Epic Status Comments** (`scripts/publish_epic_status_comments.py`) — Weekly cron (Thursdays) that reads the same rows and upserts a per-epic status comment on each epic's GitHub or Jira issue. Idempotent via a hidden `<!-- weekly-status:YYYY-MM-DD -->` marker — re-runs edit the existing comment in place. Skips rows where every human-editable cell is still a draft placeholder.

## Running Locally

```sh
# Epic hygiene check (prints to stdout when Slack creds are absent)
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) python scripts/epic_hygiene_check.py

# Draft epic status updates (requires service account JSON; use --dry-run first)
pip install -r requirements.txt
GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
GOOGLE_SHEETS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON="$(cat path/to/service-account.json)" \
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-... SLACK_BOT_CHANNEL_ID=C... \
python scripts/draft_epic_status_updates.py --dry-run
```

Most scripts use Python 3 stdlib + the `gh` CLI only. The exceptions are
the spreadsheet-touching scripts (`draft_epic_status_updates.py`,
`publish_epic_status_summary.py`, `publish_epic_status_comments.py`),
which depend on `google-auth` + `google-api-python-client` (pinned in
`requirements.txt`) for Google Sheets access — RSA JWT signing isn't
practical in stdlib alone.

## Tests

Pure-function unit tests live in `tests/`. They cover routing,
idempotency keys, status filtering, and other logic where a regression
would be user-visible (wrong recipient, duplicate row, missed epic).
Integration boundaries (gh CLI, Slack, Sheets) remain validated by
dry-runs and the workflow-dispatch flow.

```sh
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
make test    # or: pytest -v
```

CI runs `pytest` on PRs and pushes to `main` that touch `scripts/`,
`tests/`, requirements files, or the test workflow.

## Architecture

- Scripts use `gh api graphql` (subprocess) to query GitHub Projects V2 API — this handles auth via `GH_TOKEN` env var.
- Slack posting uses `urllib.request` directly (no SDK).
- Pagination: cursor-based, 100 items per page. Pass cursor via `gh api graphql -F cursor=VALUE` (not `-f variables=JSON`, which silently ignores the cursor).
- GitHub Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` does **not** have Projects V2 scope — a PAT (`GH_PROJECTS_TOKEN` secret) is required.

## Detailed Guides

Load the relevant guidance when appropriate to the task.

- [`docs/guides/testing-new-workflows-from-a-branch.md`](docs/guides/testing-new-workflows-from-a-branch.md) — when creating a new GitHub Actions workflow

## Key Project Board Details

- **Org**: navapbc
- **Project number**: 4 ("Strata")
- **Status field values**: New, Backlog, Blocked, Ready, Prioritized, In progress, In review, Done (with emoji prefixes)
- **Roadmap Status**: Now, Next, Later
- **Epic identification**: via GitHub's native `issueType` field (not a project custom field)

# Agent Context: Benefits Delivery System

## Project Overview

**Benefits Delivery System** is Nava's accumulated knowledge on means-tested benefits enrollment, encoded into transferable frameworks, prototypes, and reference materials.

**Co-owners:** Meghana Khandekar (Principal Designer/Researcher in Labs GSN), Kelli Ho (Principal Designer/Researcher & Solutions Architect in Growth)

## Repository Structure

```
benefits-delivery-system/
├── src/                    # React showcase app
├── frameworks/             # Core IP: three safety-net frameworks (markdown)
├── public/prototypes/      # Static HTML prototypes
├── docs/                   # Initiative, references, design ideas
│   └── references/ai-ux/   # AI UX patterns; provenance: how-ai-ux-patterns-were-created.md
└── server/                 # Express API stub
```

## Key Patterns

### Config-Driven Content
All framework and prototype entries are defined in `src/config/frameworks.ts` and `src/config/prototypes.ts`. Adding content = one object in the array.

### Two CSS Worlds
- **Showcase site:** Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui
- **Prototypes:** USWDS 3.x tokens or custom CSS (intentionally separate)

### Asset Paths
Use `assetUrl(...)` from `src/lib/assets.ts` for public assets. Never hard-code root-relative paths.

## Common Commands

```bash
npm run dev:client    # Showcase site + prototypes
npm run dev           # Full stack (client + API)
npm run test:run      # Run tests
```

## Critical Reminders

1. **Read before edit** — always read existing patterns before making changes
2. **Config files are source of truth** — don't hard-code framework/prototype data in components
3. **Prototypes are static** — they live in `public/` and are served as-is
4. **Frameworks are markdown** — readable on GitHub, editable by non-engineers
5. **Import from `"react-router"`** — not `"react-router-dom"` (not installed)

## Learned User Preferences

- Keep one canonical Claude Code preview command doc per flow (`/preview` → `.claude/commands/preview.md`); avoid overlapping duplicate command files for the same npm scripts.
- **Issue tracker: GitHub Issues only.** The team (Meghana + Kelli) uses GitHub Issues at `navapbc/benefits-delivery-system`. Jira was created but the team decided against it.
- When drafting public-facing content (channel updates, PR descriptions), do NOT include: DM-sourced intel, named individual stances from relay sources (e.g., "Harlan is aligned: his position is..."), or details about other teams' work not yet shared with those teams' leadership.
- In external communications, frame collaboration around strategic value ("why it matters") rather than meeting-by-meeting outcomes.
- When removing sensitive specifics from a draft, don't over-correct to vague abstractions — find the right altitude: specific enough to convey real capability, without exposing private details or names.

## Learned Workspace Facts

- `npm run preview:reset` (client + prototypes) and `npm run preview:reset:full` (client + API) run `.claude/scripts/preview-reset.sh`, which stops listeners on `BF_CLIENT_PORT` / `BF_API_PORT` (defaults **5173** / **3001**) then starts `dev:client` or `dev`.
- Vite `server.host` reads `BF_VITE_HOST` from the environment (see `vite.config.ts`); use it when binding `0.0.0.0` fails or you want localhost-only.
- Prototype URLs are `/prototypes/<folder>/index.html` where `<folder>` is a real directory name under `public/prototypes/` (not literal angle brackets).
- Extra cloned repos inside the workspace: keep them out of the parent repo's tracked tree unless intentional (e.g. add to `.gitignore`).
- The repo was renamed from `benefits-foundations` to `benefits-delivery-system` in May 2026 (PRs #17-18). GitHub repo is `navapbc/benefits-delivery-system`.
- Ed Mullen is an internal ally and exec whisperer for BDS — not an exec sponsor. His guidance arrives via DMs with Meghana and Kelli and should not be attributed or quoted in public-facing content.

# Claude Instructions for Benefits Delivery System

## Hard Rules

- **Observe, never infer.** When reporting state, run a read-only check (`ls`, `git status`, `grep`, read the file) before claiming results. Do not infer file existence or contents from prior knowledge or training data.
- **Read whole documents before editing.** Confirm the target is the canonical copy (check `docs/initiative/` first for BDS/MGR concepts). Never edit a stale or duplicate copy.
- **Never use `--no-verify`** to bypass pre-commit or commit hooks without explicit human approval.
- **Never force-push to `main`.**

### Branching and merging (hard, no exceptions)

- **Never push directly to `main`.** All work — code, docs, one-line fixes — goes through a branch + PR. No exceptions.
- **Branch from `main` using the prefix convention in `CONTRIBUTING.md`** (`docs/`, `feat/`, `fix/`, `chore/`). Never reuse a merged branch for new work.
- **Never merge a PR I authored without explicit per-PR approval from the user.** "Merge PR #N" is scoped to #N only — it does NOT extend to subsequent PRs. Each PR requires its own decision. The default after `gh pr create` is to surface the URL and stop.
- **Never invoke `gh pr merge` (with or without `--auto`).** The `--auto` flag waits for CI; it is NOT a substitute for user approval. Treat the command as off-limits unless the user has explicitly instructed merge for that specific PR in that specific turn.
- **After a PR opens or merges, do not return to `main` and start new work autonomously.** Wait for the next direction. Don't loop branch → PR → merge → main → branch.

---

## Key Files

- `src/config/frameworks.ts` — single source of truth for all framework entries
- `src/config/prototypes.ts` — single source of truth for all prototype entries
- `src/pages/IndexPage.tsx` — home page (framework cards + prototype gallery)
- `src/pages/FrameworkDetailPage.tsx` — per-framework detail page
- `src/pages/PrototypeViewerPage.tsx` — per-prototype detail page
- `src/components/SiteHeader.tsx` — site-wide header
- `frameworks/` — core IP: three safety-net frameworks (markdown)
- `public/prototypes/` — static HTML prototypes served as-is
- `docs/initiative/` — Benefits Delivery System proposal
- `memory.md` — persistent repo learnings
- `docs/architecture.md` — architectural rules. Enforced by tests in `src/test/arch/`.

---

## Running the App Locally

### Client Only (default for most work)

```bash
npm run dev:client
```

- Showcase site on `http://localhost:5173`
- Prototypes accessible at `http://localhost:5173/prototypes/co-snap-hybrid/index.html`

### Full Stack (when AI-first prototype needs API)

```bash
npm run dev
```

Runs client + Express API server concurrently.

---

## Repo Memory

When referencing anything from `public/` in app code, use `assetUrl(...)` from `src/lib/assets.ts` instead of hard-coded `/...` paths. The site may not be served from the domain root.

---

## Front-End Coding Rules

**Follow these rules exactly when adding or modifying styles in this codebase.**

### Tech Stack

- **Router:** React Router v7 — always import from `"react-router"`
- **CSS Framework:** Tailwind CSS v4
- **Component Library:** shadcn/ui (Radix primitives + Tailwind)
- **Theming:** CSS custom properties in `src/styles/globals.css`, mapped to Tailwind via `@theme inline`
- **Icons:** Lucide React

### Spacing Rules

**USE Tailwind spacing classes directly. DO NOT create CSS variables or TypeScript objects for spacing.**

```tsx
// CORRECT
className="p-4 gap-2 space-y-4 mt-6"

// WRONG
className="p-[18px] gap-[10px] mt-[24px]"
```

### Color Rules

**Colors use CSS custom properties. Reference via Tailwind classes.**

```tsx
// CORRECT
className="bg-primary text-primary-foreground"

// WRONG
style={{ backgroundColor: '#946B52' }}
```

### Prototype Rules

Prototypes in `public/prototypes/` are static files served as-is. They have their own CSS systems (USWDS tokens, custom CSS) that are intentionally separate from the showcase site's Tailwind/shadcn setup.

When adding a new prototype:
1. Place files in `public/prototypes/your-name/`
2. Add an entry to `src/config/prototypes.ts`
3. The prototype is served at `/prototypes/your-name/`

### Accessibility Rules

All interactive elements MUST have visible focus indicators. Icon-only buttons MUST have `aria-label`.

---

## Document Editing Rules

Before editing any document:
1. Read the **entire** target file — no partial reads, no relying on prior context or agent summaries.
2. If the target doc isn't explicitly named, ask which file before touching anything.
3. Read `docs/initiative/` before writing about any BDS framework concept — canonical definitions live there, not in assumptions.

---

## Verification Rules

**Always observe, never infer state.**

After any `mv`, `rm`, `git rm`, or destructive operation — run a read-only check (`ls`, `git status`, `find`) on the affected area before reporting results to the user.

When a file path comes from tool output (e.g. `git worktree list`) — verify with `find` before trusting it.

To move files: use `mv`, not read + write + delete.

**Check the diff, not just the diff-stat.** When a batch hook auto-fixes files, `git diff --stat` tells you the shape (`+107/-107`) but not which hook ran or what actually changed. Read `git diff` on a representative file before describing the change in a commit message — inaccurate descriptions compound into hard-to-search history.

---

## Session Protocol

**At session start:**
1. Read `CLAUDE.md` (this file), `memory.md`, and the most recent session retro in `docs/sessions/`.
2. Run `git status` and `git log -5` to see what changed since the last session.
3. If a plan is being executed, read the active plan doc in `docs/plans/` before suggesting next steps.
4. **Before building any automation** (hooks, commands, skills, or workflow changes in `.claude/`): run `git fetch origin && git log HEAD..origin/main --oneline -- .claude/ docs/plans/` to check for relevant main commits this branch doesn't have. If there are hits, read them before proceeding.

**During the session:**
- Write a session retro to `docs/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-NN-short-title.md` for any session that ships a PR, makes a decision worth recording, or surfaces a lesson. Use frontmatter: `date`, `session`, `title`, `participants`.
- Apply the Content Sensitivity rules below before committing session docs — they get pushed.

**Carry-forward:**
- Open items live in the active plan doc (`docs/plans/`), not in session retros. Session retros record what *was* done; plans record what *needs* doing.
- Don't open a session by re-explaining what's already in the retros or plan. Skim them silently and proceed.

**Plan file location (hard rule):**
- Any plan, review, or strategic doc lives at `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md` in the repo.
- Never in `~/.claude/plans/` (Claude Code's local plan-mode storage). If plan mode requires a file there, that file is a one-line redirect pointing at the repo doc.
- Reason: repo docs are discoverable by Kelli, Joe, future SMEs. `~/.claude/plans/` is user-local, invisible to the team, and lost between machines.

---

## Content Sensitivity

Sensitive content slips into files that DO get pushed: session docs, MGRs, GitHub issue bodies, PR descriptions, commit messages. The `private-*/` glob in `.gitignore` handles the storage side. These rules handle the output side.

**Categories of content never to push:**
- Colleague-attribution ("X's feedback wasn't incorporated," "Y disagreed with the call").
- Specific sensitive labels naming the nature of internal content.
- Exec-prep specifics (stakeholder names + internal framing).
- Anything live-attributed to a named external party without consent.
- Credentials (tokens, PATs, API keys, base64 chunks ≥40 chars in prose contexts).

**Stay one category higher than feels natural.** Stop at the abstract category — "sensitive content" or "internal-only content" — never an adjective in front of it ("X-named docs," "feedback docs"). Adjectives re-leak the dimension the abstraction was meant to protect. **Self-correction trigger:** if an adjective sits in front of "content"/"docs"/"issue," ask whether it's required for technical clarity; if not, cut it.

**Scrub-before-push window.** The post-commit, pre-push window is the only cheap opportunity to rewrite history. Once pushed, force-push to scrub becomes irresponsible. Prefer interactive rewrite over forward-only `private-*/` move when uncertain.

**`git rm` is forward-only.** Removing tracked sensitive files stops future exposure but does NOT erase history. Treat history scrubbing as a separately-reviewed operation, not bundled with cleanup work.

**Credentials are sensitive content.** Tokens, PATs, API keys, and similar strings briefly visible in conversation must be **revoked**, not trusted to remain private. Rotation is cheap; relying on the conversation being unindexed is not.

**Pre-push verification.** Before pushing, scan the diff with:
```bash
git diff origin/main..HEAD | grep -iE "gh[ps]_|sk-|ghp_|password|secret|token|exec-demo|exec-prep|colleague|feedback (from|by)"
```
If anything matches, treat as a content-sensitivity event before push.

---

## Writing Rules

All prose in this repo (READMEs, MGRs, session retros, PR descriptions, commit messages, plan docs) follows `docs/writing-style-guide.md`. Read it once; the rules below are the load-bearing summary.

**Plain-language defaults (plain-language.gov standard):**
- **Full Name (ACRONYM)** on first mention, never the reverse. `Government Services Navigator (GSN)` is correct; `GSN (Government Services Navigator)` is not.
- Common words over jargon. See the Latinate alternatives table in `docs/writing-style-guide.md`.
- Active voice.

**Universal principles:**
- Lead with what IS, not what isn't.
- Close every loop — every limitation has a named response.
- Concrete over abstract. Match vocabulary to the reader's job.
- Each sentence earns the next.
- Omit needless words.
- Evidence before claims — don't soften or hedge until the claim disappears.
- Verify attributions before writing them.

**Definitional consistency:**
- When a concept (MGR, BDS) is described in more than one place, every description must reconcile to one canonical structure. The 6 knowledge-base content categories ≠ the 5 MGR per-record layers — label them as different views, never collapse the counts.
- When a string is renamed (e.g., "IE&E Starter Kit" → "Benefits Delivery System"), distinguish initiative-name uses from industry-term uses.

**Structural rules:**
- One rhetorical move per document. "Not X, it's Y" once max.
- Tables for reference, prose for arguments.
- Watch for restated content across adjacent sections.
- Stakes-led openings over description-led for READMEs and PR descriptions.
- Always grep wider than the named locations when fixing a rename.
- Categorize grep results (delete / edit / keep / false-positive) before acting.

**Link and attribution rules:**
- Links go on source names, not category labels. `[the MGR1 file](path)` not `[the file](path)`.
- No fabricated quotes; no placeholder language (`[TODO]`, `[X]`) except where actually a placeholder — track in TodoWrite or as an issue.

**Banned AI words / phrases (cut on sight):**
- Words: delve, tapestry, realm, foster, landscape, leverage, robust, seamless, navigate, journey, embark, multifaceted, nuanced, comprehensive, intricate, pivotal, paramount, crucial, underscore, showcase, illuminate, unveil, harness, elevate, unlock, streamline, optimize, cutting-edge, groundbreaking, game-changer, testament, meticulous, unwavering, invaluable, vibrant, dynamic, innovative, notably, particularly.
- Phrases: "Let's delve into," "In today's fast-paced world," "It's worth mentioning that," "Moreover," / "Furthermore," / "Additionally," "Looking ahead," "Despite these challenges," "I hope this email finds you well," "In conclusion."
- Structural anti-patterns: tacked-on -ing phrases ("...highlighting the importance of X"), significance/legacy language ("marking a pivotal moment"), rhetorical question transitions ("The result?" / "The takeaway?"), em-dash overuse, "everything is crucial" inflation, no-committed-position seesawing.
- No section-opening "I/we'll" filler.

See `docs/writing-style-guide.md` for the full guide including examples and the quick-reference checklist.

---

## Framework Content Rules

Frameworks in `frameworks/` are markdown. They should be:
- Readable on GitHub directly (no build step)
- Editable by non-engineers
- Cross-referenced accurately (update links when moving files)

See `frameworks/CLAUDE.md` for MGR-specific rules (frontmatter, naming, canonical source).

---

## File Ownership

When a new rule, fact, or convention lands, it goes in one place. Here is the map:

| File                          | Owns                                                                  | Updated when             |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `CLAUDE.md` (this file)       | Behavioral rules for Claude; load-bearing summaries                   | A new rule is added      |
| `AGENTS.md`                   | Team coordination context                                             | Team workflow changes    |
| `memory.md` + `memory/`       | Repo-visible team learnings. `memory.md` is the index; `memory/*.md` holds the content (`repo-facts.md`, `verification.md`, `gotchas.md`, `dso-removal.md`) | A learning happens that the team should see |
| `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/` | Claude session-feedback patterns (user-local, not team-visible)    | Claude is corrected      |
| `docs/architecture.md`        | Architectural rules — operational summary + enforcement              | Architectural changes    |
| `docs/adr/`                   | Architecture Decision Records — formal record per rule (context, alternatives) | A new rule lands or an existing rule changes materially |
| `docs/workflows.md`           | Index of all automated + manual workflows in the repo (hooks, slash commands, CI, pre-commit) — read this when something runs you didn't expect | A hook, command, CI job, or pre-commit hook is added, removed, or changed |
| `docs/writing-style-guide.md` | Prose style rules for all repo writing                                | A new pattern surfaces in PR review |
| `docs/plans/`                 | Dated plan docs (`YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`). Active plans drive ongoing work; archived plans are historical record. Template: `docs/plans/_template.md` | A new plan is written, or a plan's status changes (draft → living → archived) |
| `docs/sessions/`              | Session retros (`YYYY-MM-DD-NN-<title>.md`). What was done in a session — decisions, mistakes, lessons. Template: `docs/sessions/_template.md` | At the end of any session that ships a PR, makes a decision worth recording, or surfaces a lesson |
| `docs/initiative/`            | Canonical concept definitions for Benefits Delivery System (what BDS is, what MGRs are, program scope). Read here first before writing about BDS concepts elsewhere | Strategic framing changes, a canonical concept is renamed or redefined |
| `docs/references/`            | Stable research and reference material — the evidence base MGRs draw on. Read-only sources                | New research is added or synthesized; existing references are not edited in place |
| `frameworks/`                 | Core IP — Model Guidance Records (MGRs) and supporting framework docs. Schema-validated. Template: `frameworks/_template/mgr-template.md` | A new MGR lands, an existing MGR's frontmatter or decision changes |
| Folder-scoped `CLAUDE.md` files | Folder-specific conventions (extend root, do not replace) | A folder gets specific rules a new contributor needs to follow |
| `.claude/skills/bds-lifecycle/SKILL.md` | Lifecycle system skill — canonical templates, rigor tiers, significance heuristics, "when to surface what" contract, disagreement protocol, self-check rubric. Auto-loads on plan/retro/memory work | Lifecycle conventions change or new self-check rules surface |
| `docs/initiative/lifecycle-onboarding.md` | Onboarding doc for the lifecycle system — paste-blocks for terminal setup + Claude verification. Discoverable for new contributors (Kelli, Joe, future SMEs) | Lifecycle setup steps change |

**Folder-scoped CLAUDE.md files exist in:** `frameworks/`, `public/prototypes/`, `docs/plans/`, `docs/sessions/`, `docs/initiative/`, `docs/references/`. Each inherits from this file; read both when editing in those folders.

**Doc frontmatter common-minimum:** every doc in `docs/` and `frameworks/` and the repo root opens with `doc-type`, `status`, and `updated`. Per-type extensions are documented in `docs/plans/2026-05-20-doc-frontmatter-alignment.md`. Folder-scoped `CLAUDE.md` files are the only exception — they inherit context and have no frontmatter.

**Decision:** `memory.md` is canonical for **team-visible** repo learnings. User-local project memory (`~/.claude/projects/.../memory/`) holds Claude-specific feedback that is identity-bound and not team-relevant. When in doubt: if a SME would benefit from reading it, write to `memory.md`.

---

## One Workflow

There is one PR-based workflow in this repo. No second pipeline.

- **Code changes** → `npm run typecheck` + `npm run test:run` (includes `src/test/arch/` fitness tests) + pre-commit gate.
- **Markdown / MGR changes** → pre-commit gate only (tsc still runs as a guard but won't see markdown).
- **All changes** → branch from `main`, PR, squash-merge after 1 approval.

CI re-runs the same checks the pre-commit gate runs. There is no separate sprint orchestration, ticket tracker, or sub-agent dispatch. `/plan-review` is a custom slash command available for design and plan reviews.

---
name: retro-drafter
description: Drafts a session retrospective by reading the session transcript JSONL + recent retros + the docs/sessions/ folder CLAUDE.md. Use when SessionEnd hook detects a high-confidence significance signal (shipped PR, plan archived, decision logged, ExitPlanMode + plan file edit) and a retro should be written. Returns a summary; the retro itself is written to disk at docs/sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-NN-<auto-title>.md with status: draft.
tools: Read, Glob, Bash, Write
model: sonnet
---

You are the retro-drafter for the BDS lifecycle system. Your job is to read a session transcript and write a draft session retrospective. The user reviews the draft and runs `/retro-finalize` to flip `status: draft` → `status: stable`.

## Inputs you'll receive

When invoked, you'll be told:
- The path to the session transcript JSONL (typically `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-id>.jsonl`)
- The detected significance signal (e.g., `shipped-pr`, `plan-archived`, `decision-logged`)
- Today's date (YYYY-MM-DD)

If not given, find the most recent JSONL in `~/.claude/projects/$(echo $PWD | sed 's|/|-|g')/` via Glob.

## Steps

1. **Read the transcript.** Use Read on the JSONL path. Each line is a JSON event with `message` (with `role` and `content`). Extract: user messages, assistant responses, tool calls, tool results.

2. **Read the folder conventions.** Read `docs/sessions/CLAUDE.md` for required sections + frontmatter format.

3. **Read the most recent retro for style.** Use Glob `docs/sessions/2026-*.md` to find the latest. Read its first 50 lines for voice/structure reference. Do NOT copy content.

4. **Determine the next NN.** Use Glob `docs/sessions/<TODAY>-*.md` to count today's existing retros. NN = (count + 1) zero-padded to 2 digits.

5. **Auto-title.** Pick 3–6 kebab-case words describing the session's most prominent topic. Sources for the title (in order of preference):
   - The shipped PR's title (if `shipped-pr` signal)
   - The archived plan's filename (if `plan-archived` signal)
   - The decision's heading text (if `decision-logged` signal)
   - The dominant topic across user messages

6. **Draft the retro.** Required sections per the folder CLAUDE.md:
   - `Session arc` — numbered list of what was done, in order
   - `What was built / decided` — specific artifacts with file paths and PR numbers
   - `Mistakes and corrections` — what went wrong, root cause, going-forward rule
   - `What's left` — open items (these get routed to plans/memory/drop by `action-promoter` in v2)
   - `Lessons worth keeping` — durable lessons (these get routed to memory by `memory-miner` in v2)

7. **Frontmatter.** Open with:
   ```yaml
   ---
   doc-type: session-retro
   status: draft
   updated: <TODAY>
   date: <TODAY>
   title: <Auto-titled, human-readable>
   participants: MK + Claude
   ---
   ```

8. **Append session-id marker** at the very end of the body as an HTML comment for idempotency:
   ```html
   <!-- session-id: <full-session-id-from-jsonl-filename> -->
   ```

9. **Write the file.** Path: `docs/sessions/<TODAY>-<NN>-<auto-title>.md`. Use Write.

10. **Apply content sensitivity rules** before writing. From `CLAUDE.md`:
    - No colleague attribution that implies judgment (e.g., "X was wrong"). Neutral attribution is fine ("X's analysis covered three patterns").
    - No exec-prep specifics + stakeholder names.
    - No credentials. Use placeholders like `ghp_REDACTED` if a credential pattern is being documented.
    - Stay one category higher than feels natural. "Sensitive content" not "X's feedback."

## Idempotency

Before writing, check via Glob/Read whether a retro for this session-id already exists. If `<!-- session-id: <id> -->` appears in any `docs/sessions/2026-*.md` file, return:

```
A retro for this session already exists: <path>. No new draft written.
```

## Output back to main session

Return a one-line summary to the calling hook:

```
Draft retro at <path>. Run /retro-finalize after review.
```

Do NOT return the retro contents — they live on disk; the main session reads them on demand.

## Log the action

Before returning, log the action via Bash:

```bash
python3 .claude/lib/lifecycle_log.py write retro-drafter <signal> <confidence> drafted-retro <path>
```

## Hard rules

- **Never overwrite an existing retro.** If the target path exists, append `-v2`, `-v3`, etc. to the filename.
- **Never write `status: stable`.** That's the user's call via `/retro-finalize`.
- **Never include action items that look like new plan-mode work** in the retro — that's `action-promoter`'s job in v2. In v1, just list them under "What's left."
- **Apply the content-sensitivity grep before writing.** If your draft contains a credential-shaped string, replace with a placeholder.

## Example invocation

```
You are being invoked by SessionEnd hook. Transcript: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-mk-foo/abc123.jsonl. Signal: shipped-pr (high). Today: 2026-05-21. Draft a retro.
```

You then read the transcript, draft the retro with the 5 required sections, write to `docs/sessions/2026-05-21-NN-<title>.md`, log the action, and return the one-line summary.

# AGENTS.md

These instructions apply to the entire repository.

## Project Context

Portico is an open source, AI-assisted federal experience modernization framework. It bridges USWDS foundations with National Design Studio (NDS)-inspired federal design expectations through reusable Tailwind-based implementation patterns, CMS-agnostic theming accelerators, Drupal implementation support, and accessibility-first delivery guidance.

The repository is early-stage. The current source of truth is the root `README.md`, the files under `docs/`, and the walkthrough artifacts under `walkthrough/`. If older walkthrough method artifacts conflict with the root README, prefer the current root README unless the user explicitly says otherwise.

Use the Google Doc "Federal Experience Modernization Framework" for additional project guidance:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CW2Za2d91DJzchtFYelTs2VREN4MTSOjyXJBv-5zX90/edit?tab=t.0

Do not treat the current walkthrough as production framework code. It is source material for the operating model, examples, implementation guidance, and future package structure.

## Core Priorities

- Accessibility is non-negotiable.
- USWDS compatibility comes before visual novelty.
- Tailwind is an implementation accelerator, not a replacement for semantic HTML, USWDS behavior, or accessibility requirements.
- Patterns should be CMS-agnostic by default.
- Drupal is a first-class implementation target.
- AI-assisted outputs must be human-reviewed and validated before being treated as authoritative.
- Governance checks should prevent token drift, arbitrary variants, accessibility regressions, and divergence from canonical patterns.
- Keep the project framed around modernization, accessibility, and implementation maturity; avoid administration-specific branding.
- Keep scope focused on an implementation framework, not a wholly new design ecosystem.
- Keep changes small, direct, and aligned with the requested task.

## Repository Workflow

- Inspect the repository before editing.
- Read active `AGENTS.md` files before making assumptions.
- Use `rg` or `rg --files` for searches.
- Use non-interactive commands.
- Use non-interactive git diff commands such as `git --no-pager diff`.
- Do not revert unrelated changes.
- Do not use destructive git commands unless the user explicitly asks for them.
- If the worktree is dirty, assume existing changes are user changes and work around them.
- Run relevant validation after code or documentation changes when the repository defines a validation path.

## Code Style

- Comments must be in English.
- Prefer pure functions. Do not mutate input parameters or global state.
- Follow DRY, KISS, and YAGNI principles.
- Use strict typing everywhere when a typed language is introduced.
- Check whether logic already exists before writing new code.
- Avoid untyped variables and generic catch-all types.
- Do not use default parameter values; make required values explicit.
- Create proper type definitions for complex data structures.
- Keep imports at the top of the file.
- Write simple single-purpose functions.
- Avoid multi-mode functions and flag parameters that switch behavior.

## Error Handling

- Raise errors explicitly.
- Use specific error types when the language supports them.
- Avoid catch-all exception handlers that hide root causes.
- Error messages should be clear and actionable.
- Do not add fallbacks unless the user explicitly asks for them.
- Fix root causes, not symptoms.
- External API or service calls should use retries with warnings, then raise the last error.
- Error messages for external calls must include useful debugging context such as request parameters, response body, and status code when available.
- Logging should use structured fields instead of interpolating dynamic values into message strings.

## Accessibility Requirements

Portico patterns are not complete until they can be validated against accessibility acceptance criteria.

At minimum, new user-facing patterns must account for:

- Semantic HTML and landmark structure.
- Keyboard operation.
- Visible focus.
- Screen reader names, roles, states, and live-region behavior where relevant.
- Color contrast for text, meaningful graphics, and UI states.
- Text resizing and browser zoom.
- Reduced motion behavior.
- Touch target size and pointer alternatives.
- Error identification, recovery, and status messaging.
- High contrast mode behavior.
- Automated checks and manual assistive technology review.

Use Section 508 as the minimum federal compliance baseline and WCAG 2.2 AA as the forward-looking project quality bar for new web patterns where applicable.

## USWDS and Tailwind Guidance

- Reuse USWDS patterns when they solve the problem.
- Preserve USWDS semantics, ARIA behavior, and interaction expectations.
- Do not override USWDS accessibility behavior without a documented reason and validation.
- Map Tailwind utilities and tokens to documented Portico or USWDS-compatible patterns.
- Prefer tokenized design values over bespoke CSS overrides.
- Keep styling layers scoped, reversible, and easy to audit.
- Document intentional divergence from USWDS.

## Governance and Risk Guidance

- Use strict token governance for color, spacing, typography, focus, states, and approved variants.
- Prefer a clear component catalog and registry over one-off implementations.
- Flag non-token values, arbitrary spacing, unauthorized component variants, accessibility regressions, and divergence from canonical patterns.
- Treat accessibility drift as a primary risk, especially in Tailwind-heavy implementations.
- Treat visual inconsistency as a primary risk when token governance is weak.
- Treat scope creep as a primary risk; prefer implementation accelerators over broad new ecosystem work.
- Frame public-facing project language around modernization, accessibility, and implementation maturity instead of administration-specific branding.

## Frontend and Example Guidance

- Build actual usable examples, not marketing pages, unless the user asks for marketing content.
- Keep examples realistic for public-sector and federal implementation contexts.
- Avoid visual treatments that interfere with trust, readability, task completion, accessibility, or rollback.
- Do not make every agency example look the same.
- Do not introduce large abstractions until reuse is proven across multiple examples or agency kits.
- When a frontend requires a local server, start it after implementation and provide the local URL.
- For static HTML that works without a server, no dev server is needed.

## Testing and Validation

- Respect the current repository testing strategy.
- This repository currently has no build system or test runner.
- Do not add unit tests by default.
- When tests are needed, prefer integration, end-to-end, accessibility, or smoke tests that validate real behavior.
- Use unit tests only for stable datasets or pure data transformations.
- Avoid mocks when real calls or real rendering are practical.
- Add governance checks when implementation work introduces tokens, component variants, Tailwind presets, examples, or canonical patterns.
- Use CI validation for linting, accessibility checks, governance checks, and example validation once project tooling exists.
- Accessibility automation is required but not sufficient; include manual validation notes when behavior depends on keyboard, screen reader, zoom, contrast, or reduced motion review.

## Documentation

- Code is the primary documentation where source code exists.
- Keep documentation close to the concepts it describes.
- Use separate docs files only when a concept cannot be expressed clearly in code or a README.
- Store knowledge as current state, not as a changelog of modifications.
- Do not duplicate documentation across files.
- Keep root README content focused on project framing, setup, architecture, roadmap, and key policies.
- Put deeper guidance in `docs/`.

## Tooling and Dependencies

- Prefer modern package management files such as `package.json` and `pyproject.toml` when tooling is introduced.
- Install dependencies in project environments, not globally.
- Add dependencies to project configuration files, not as one-off manual installs.
- Read installed dependency source code when needed instead of guessing behavior.
- Keep dependency additions justified by current project needs.

## Security

- Do not disclose vulnerabilities in public issues or public documentation.
- Follow `SECURITY.md` for vulnerability reporting.
- Do not include secrets, tokens, credentials, or private endpoint details in examples or docs.

## Git

- Use `git --no-pager diff` for diffs.
- Do not revert unrelated changes.
- Do not run destructive commands such as `git reset --hard` or `git checkout --` unless the user explicitly asks.
- Keep commits, branches, and pull requests scoped to the requested work when the user asks for git operations.

skills.author: navapbc
skills.content:
# Agent Instructions

This project uses **trekker** for issue tracking. Run `trekker quickstart` to get started.

## Quick Reference

```bash
trekker ready  # Find available work
trekker task show TREK-1          # View task details
trekker task update TREK-1 -s in_progress  # Claim work
trekker comment add TREK-1 -a "agent" -c "Summary: ..."  # Add completion comment
trekker task update TREK-1 -s completed    # Complete work
```

## Non-Interactive Shell Commands

**ALWAYS use non-interactive flags** with file operations to avoid hanging on confirmation prompts.

Shell commands like `cp`, `mv`, and `rm` may be aliased to include `-i` (interactive) mode on some systems, causing the agent to hang indefinitely waiting for y/n input.

**Use these forms instead:**
```bash
# Force overwrite without prompting
cp -f source dest           # NOT: cp source dest
mv -f source dest           # NOT: mv source dest
rm -f file                  # NOT: rm file

# For recursive operations
rm -rf directory            # NOT: rm -r directory
cp -rf source dest          # NOT: cp -r source dest
```

**Other commands that may prompt:**
- `scp` - use `-o BatchMode=yes` for non-interactive
- `ssh` - use `-o BatchMode=yes` to fail instead of prompting
- `apt-get` - use `-y` flag
- `brew` - use `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` env var

## Server Process Cleanup

**ALWAYS kill any server processes you start once you are done using them.** Do not leave background servers running after testing.

```bash
# Kill all tsx server processes when done testing
pkill -f "tsx.*server" 2>/dev/null
```

If you start a server (e.g., `PORT=4001 npx tsx apps/pfml-reference-server/src/server.ts &`) to test or verify changes, you **must** kill it before finishing your work or moving on to an unrelated task.

<!-- BEGIN TREKKER INTEGRATION -->
## Issue Tracking with trekker

**IMPORTANT**: This project uses **trekker** for ALL issue tracking. Do NOT use markdown TODOs, task lists, or other tracking methods.

### Why trekker?

- Dependency-aware: Track blockers and relationships between tasks
- Local-only SQLite DB: No server required, stored in `.trekker/trekker.db`
- Agent-optimized: Token-efficient output with `--toon` flag
- Epics, tasks, subtasks, comments, and full-text search

### Quick Start

**Check for ready work:**

```bash
trekker ready
```

**Create new tasks:**

```bash
trekker task create -t "Task title" -d "Detailed context" -p 0-5 -e EPIC-1
trekker task create -t "Found bug" -d "Details about what was found" -p 1 -e EPIC-1
```

**Claim a task:**

```bash
trekker task update TREK-1 -s in_progress
```

**Complete work (comment + status update):**

```bash
trekker comment add TREK-1 -a "agent" -c "Summary: implemented X in files A, B"
trekker task update TREK-1 -s completed
```

### Task Types (via tags)

Use tags to categorize tasks: `--tags "bug"`, `--tags "feature"`, `--tags "task"`, `--tags "chore"`

### Priorities

- `0` - Critical (security, data loss, broken builds)
- `1` - High (major features, important bugs)
- `2` - Medium (default, nice-to-have)
- `3` - Low (polish, optimization)
- `4` - Backlog (future ideas)
- `5` - Someday

### Workflow for AI Agents

1. **Check ready work**: `trekker ready` shows available tasks
2. **Claim your task**: `trekker task update TREK-1 -s in_progress`
3. **Work on it**: Implement, test, document
4. **Discover new work?** Create linked task:
   - `trekker task create -t "Found bug" -d "Details" -p 1 -e EPIC-1`
   - `trekker dep add TREK-new TREK-parent`
5. **Complete**: Add summary comment then mark completed:
   - `trekker comment add TREK-1 -a "agent" -c "Summary: what was done"`
   - `trekker task update TREK-1 -s completed`

### Important Rules

- ✅ Use trekker for ALL task tracking
- ✅ Use `--toon` flag for token-efficient output
- ✅ Add a summary comment before marking tasks complete
- ✅ Check `trekker ready` before asking "what should I work on?"
- ❌ Do NOT create markdown TODO lists
- ❌ Do NOT use external issue trackers
- ❌ Do NOT duplicate tracking systems

For full workflow details, run `trekker quickstart`.

## Landing the Plane (Session Completion)

**When ending a work session**, you MUST complete ALL steps below. Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds.

**MANDATORY WORKFLOW:**

1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create trekker tasks for anything that needs follow-up
2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
3. **Update task status** - Complete finished work, update in-progress items
4. **PUSH TO REMOTE** - This is MANDATORY:
   ```bash
   git add -A
   git pull --rebase
   git push
   git status  # MUST show "up to date with origin"
   ```
5. **Clean up** - Clear stashes, prune remote branches
6. **Verify** - All changes committed AND pushed
7. **Hand off** - Provide context for next session

**CRITICAL RULES:**
- Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds
- NEVER stop before pushing - that leaves work stranded locally
- NEVER say "ready to push when you are" - YOU must push
- If push fails, resolve and retry until it succeeds

<!-- END TREKKER INTEGRATION -->

## ERAS HTMX Fragment Convention

The ERAS app (`apps/eras`) uses HTMX OOB (out-of-band) swaps to update panels dynamically. Each partial in `apps/eras/src/views/partials/` may have a corresponding HTMX fragment in `apps/eras/src/views/_htmx-fragments/`.

**When you change a partial, you MUST also update the matching HTMX fragment.**

### Why this matters

- HTMX fragments are rendered server-side and swapped into the DOM via `hx-swap-oob="outerHTML"`.
- If the fragment markup diverges from the partial, the swapped content will be unstyled or broken.
- Styles must NOT live inside elements that get OOB-swapped — they belong in the parent page (e.g., `case-detail.ejs`) so they persist across swaps.

### Checklist when editing a partial

1. Update the HTMX fragment with matching markup/class changes
2. Ensure styles are in the parent page's `<style>` block, not inside the swappable element
3. Verify the `id` attribute used for OOB targeting still matches

# Claude Code Instructions

## What this system is (and isn't)

This repository is a **proof-of-concept demo** for NJ Department of Labor Wage & Hour Compliance case management. It is not a production enforcement system and is not connected to live state systems.

**Every case-affecting decision in this system passes through human review before any external consequence.** Workflow transitions are triggered by named human actors (CRM intake clerks, investigators, supervisors, WC referees, FIN staff); the SDK records the actor on every transition. There is no autonomous action — no automated letters mailed, no payments disbursed, no enforcement referrals filed without an authenticated human acting first.

**The decision rules are deterministic pure functions; no AI, LLM, or probabilistic classifier participates in case-affecting decisions.** The criterion evaluators (`jurisdictionEval`, `employerHistoryEval`, `employerClassificationEval`, `wageViolationEval`, `penaltyCalculationEval` under `apps/nj-wh-reference-server/src/domain/evaluators/`) are vanilla TypeScript pure functions over a typed signal map. The workflow guards (e.g. `supervisor-approved`) are deterministic boolean predicates over case state. When an evaluator returns "violation-confirmed" it is presenting a computed legal/arithmetic conclusion (e.g. *minimum wage − employer rate × hours × weeks = back wages*) for a human to review, accept, or override via the metadata-edit and supervisor-approval mechanisms.

Treat any code in `apps/nj-wh-reference-server/src/domain/` as the canonical decision logic. There is no model inference, no embedding lookup, no probability threshold anywhere in the case-management decision path. The use of AI assistants (Claude Code included) is for *implementation* of this deterministic system, not for run-time decisioning.

## Planning Requirement

When creating plans in plan mode, include an appendix that includes a transcript of the prompts that generated the plan.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Overview

This is the Maryland DOL FAMLI Infrastructure repository containing Terraform code and GitHub Actions workflows for managing AWS infrastructure across multiple environments. The team follows Trunk-based development with continuous deployment to staging and manual promotion to production.

## Architecture

### Multi-Account AWS Structure

- **Non-production account**: Contains staging and sandbox environments (sb1-sb7)
- **Production account**: Separate AWS account for production environment
- State is stored in S3 with DynamoDB locking, separate per environment

### Repository Structure

- **`terraform/environment/`**: Separate root modules for each environment (staging, production, sb1-sb7). Each is fully independent with its own state backend.
- **`terraform/modules/`**: Reusable Terraform modules (35+ modules) shared across environments. These are designed to be potentially open-sourced.
- **`terraform/account/`**: Account-level bootstrap configuration for setting up S3 state backends and base IAM. These must be applied locally by DevOps engineers, not via CI/CD.
- **`terraform/integration/`**: Integration-specific modules (e.g. external services, datadog, github-runner)

## Important Patterns

### Providers

- Standard AWS provider has default tags (Terraform, env, TerraformModulePath)
- `aws.no_tags` alias for resources with immutable tags
- Datadog provider configured via AWS Secrets Manager

### State Management

Each environment root module has its own S3 backend configuration in `init.tf`:
```hcl
backend "s3" {
  region         = "us-east-1"
  bucket         = "tf-state-ACCOUNT_ID"
  key            = "environment/<env-name>/terraform.tfstate"
  dynamodb_table = "TerraformStateLock"
}
```

### Module Documentation

All modules in `terraform/modules/` and `terraform/integration/` must have auto-generated documentation. The `.terraform-docs.yml` file at the repository root configures the format. **Do not** place `.terraform-docs.yml` files in individual module directories.

## CI/CD Workflows

Key workflows in `.github/workflows/`:
- `deploy.yml`: Main deployment workflow (auto-deploy to staging, manual for others)
- `terraform-plan.yml`: Reusable workflow that runs plan in PR checks
- `infra-pr.yml`: Runs plan for all changed environments in a PR
- `on-push-main-autodeploy-integration.yml`: Auto-deploys integration environments
- `scheduled_deploy.yml`: Scheduled deployments
- `static-analysis.yml`: Runs linting and security checks

## Key Constraints

- `main` branch must always be deployable to production
- Account-level Terraform (`terraform/account/`) cannot run in CI/CD - must be applied locally by DevOps
- Never use Terraform workspaces - use separate root modules instead
- All module documentation must be generated via terraform-docs, not manually written

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Repository structure

The Rails application lives in `reporting-app/`. **All `make` commands below must be run from that subdirectory**, not the repo root.

```
reporting-app/    # Rails 8.0 app (Ruby 3.4.9)
infra/            # Terraform infrastructure
e2e/              # Playwright end-to-end tests (TypeScript)
docs/             # Architecture & feature docs
  architecture/   # Feature-specific ADRs (batch-upload, doc-ai, staff-sso, va-eligibility, etc.)
  reporting-app/  # App-level docs (auth, forms, i18n, security, jobs, lookbook)
```

## Commands

```bash
# Development
make start-native          # Run app locally (Procfile.dev)
make start-container       # Run via Docker
make init-native           # First-time setup (native)
make rails-console         # Rails console
make rails-routes          # Show all routes
make clear-cache           # Clear Rails cache and assets
make precompile-assets     # Precompile asset pipeline

# Testing
make test                             # Full test suite
make test args="spec/path/to/file.rb" # Single file

# Database
make db-migrate        # Run pending migrations
make db-rollback       # Rollback last migration
make db-seed           # Seed data
make db-reset          # Drop, recreate from schema.rb, reseed
make db-test-prepare   # Prepare test database
make db-up             # Start just the database container
make db-console        # PostgreSQL console

# Code generation (always pass --primary-key-type=uuid)
make rails-generate GENERATE_COMMAND="model Foo --primary-key-type=uuid"
make rails-generate GENERATE_COMMAND="migration AddColumnToFoos column:type"
make rails-generate GENERATE_COMMAND="scaffold Foo --primary-key-type=uuid"

# Locales & authorization
make locale                          # Generate locale files for a model
make new-authz-policy MODEL=Foo      # Generate Pundit policy

# API documentation
make openapi-spec      # Generate OpenAPI YAML spec

# Code quality
make lint       # RuboCop with auto-fix
```

## Bounded contexts

- **Certifications** – `Certification` (aggregate root) → `CertificationCase` → `Activities`, `InformationRequests`, `Determination`
- **Certification Batch Uploads** – `CertificationBatchUpload` → `CertificationBatchUploadAuditLog`, `CertificationBatchUploadError`; async chunked processing via GoodJob
- **Activity Reporting** – `ActivityReportApplicationForm` → `Activity` (STI: `HourlyActivity`, `IncomeActivity`, `WorkActivity`, `ExternalHourlyActivity`) → `ActivityReportInformationRequest`
- **Exemptions** – `ExemptionApplicationForm` → `Exemption` → `ExemptionInformationRequest`; rules engine via `Rules::ExemptionRuleset`
- **Document AI (DocAI)** – `StagedDocument` (pending → validated → rejected → failed) → `DocAiResult` (value object with `Payslip` subclass); confidence scoring, payslip-to-activity pre-fill. Feature-flagged via `FEATURE_DOC_AI`
- **External Hourly Activities** – `ExternalHourlyActivity` with source tracking (batch upload vs. API); imported via batch or VA integration
- **Tasks** – `OscerTask` (extends `Strata::Task`), `ReviewActivityReportTask`, `ReviewExemptionClaimTask` – polymorphic work items for staff
- **Auth** – `User` (Devise) with triple login: member form, member OIDC (`MemberOidcController`), staff SSO (`Auth::SsoController`)
- **VA Integration** – `VeteranAffairsAdapter` → `VeteranDisabilityService` for eligibility/disability data
- **Notifications** – `NotificationService` + `NotificationsEventListener` (event-driven via Strata pub/sub) → `MemberMailer` (AWS SES)

## Development workflow

1. **Ask clarifying questions** before writing code — never assume business logic
2. **Write RSpec tests first**, present for approval, then implement
3. After passing tests: `make lint` then `make test`

- `docs/reporting-app/software-architecture.md` — architecture patterns

- `docs/reporting-app/forms.md` — USWDS form helper reference

- `docs/reporting-app/background-jobs.md` — GoodJob configuration
- `docs/reporting-app/api.md` — API documentation

npx jest tests/backend/IdeaService.test.ts

npx jest tests/backend/IdeaService.test.ts -t "create"
